data.title: Distance Problem
data.statement:
You need to take a group photo of both Alice's class and Bob's class, with the students arranged in a single line.

Alice's class consists of n students, indexed from 1 to n, while Bob's class consists of m students, indexed from 1 to m.

Each student has an "uncomfortable index" associated with them.

For each student in Alice's class, the uncomfortable index (denoted as Ai) is calculated as Ai multiplied by the absolute difference between the number of Bob's classmates to the left (L) and to the right (R) of that student. If a student is standing at index 1, the value of L is 0. Similarly, if a student is standing at index n, the value of R is 0.

Similarly, for each student in Bob's class, the uncomfortable index (denoted as Bj) is calculated as Bj multiplied by the absolute difference between the number of Alice's classmates to the left (L) and to the right (R) of that student. L is the number of opposite-class students to the left of the student in the full lineup. R is the number to the right.

Your task is to find the optimal arrangement of all (n + m) students that minimizes the sum of their uncomfortable indices.
Note that the answer may not fit in a 32-bit data type.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

You need to take a group photo of both Alice's class and Bob's class, with the students arranged in a single line.

Alice's class consists of n students, indexed from 1 to n, while Bob's class consists of m students, indexed from 1 to m.

Each student has an "uncomfortable index" associated with them.

For each student in Alice's class, the uncomfortable index (denoted as Ai) is calculated as Ai multiplied by the absolute difference between the number of Bob's classmates to the left (L) and to the right (R) of that student. If a student is standing at index 1, the value of L is 0. Similarly, if a student is standing at index n, the value of R is 0.

Similarly, for each student in Bob's class, the uncomfortable index (denoted as Bj) is calculated as Bj multiplied by the absolute difference between the number of Alice's classmates to the left (L) and to the right (R) of that student. L is the number of opposite-class students to the left of the student in the full lineup. R is the number to the right.

Your task is to find the optimal arrangement of all (n + m) students that minimizes the sum of their uncomfortable indices.
Note that the answer may not fit in a 32-bit data type.
Input
Line 1: n m, 2 positive integers space-separated, denoting the amount of students in Alice's and Bob's classes respectively.
Line 2: n integers (A1 to An), denoting the uncomfortable index of each student in Alice's class, space-separated.
Line 3: m integers (B1 to Bm), denoting the uncomfortable index of each student in Bob's class, space-separated.
Output
Print the minimal sum of all students' uncomfortable index by rearranging all (n + m) students optimally.
Constraints
1 <= n, m <= 500
1 <= Ai, Bi <= 10^9
Example
Input
5 7
522 575 426 445 772
81 447 629 497 202 775 325
Output
13354
